statement: Other differences: The elapsed time between A03 and A13 completions decreased substantially, from a median of about 168 hours to about 66 hours. This is a separate timing change; it is based on a single item and could be related to the resource reallocation or to other factors, but it is not needed for the resource-allocation hypothesis. [TWAIT001]

For activity A16, the change is extreme: before, 19 distinct resources handled it, with the top resource at 18.2%; after, only one resource (User_64) handled 100% of the work. The concentration index went from 0.094 to 1.0. [ASSIGN005, CONC001]

Resource allocation changed for several activities. For A01, A03, A13, A14, and A17, the share of work done by User_56 increased from 0% to about 11–12% (e.g., A01: 0% to 11.5%, A03: 0% to 12.1%, A13/A14: 0% to 10.3%, A17: 0% to 11.1%), and User_46 also increased (e.g., A01: 0% to 6.5%, A03: 0% to 6.5%, A13/A14: 0% to 6.9%, A17: 0% to 7.4%). Meanwhile, User_3, User_10, User_41, User_51, User_57, and User_58 decreased or disappeared. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN003, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN006]

Other differences: The elapsed time between A04 and A01 increased substantially in the later window (median from ~5.6 to ~17.6 hours). This is a separate timing change, supported by one time item (TWAIT001) against 0.012 expected by chance. [TWAIT001]

In the later window, after activity A10, the share of transitions to A16 decreased from about 57% to 44%, while transitions to A07 increased from 10% to 24%; A11 decreased from 17% to 11%, A19 disappeared, and A13 appeared. [DIR001]

In the later window, resource allocation for activities A01, A03, A13, A14, A17, and A22 shifted from a broad pool of many resources (each with small shares, plus a large "OTHER" share around 50%) to a smaller set: User_3 increased from near 0% to about 12–15% of assignments, User_78 and User_61 appeared with shares around 6–9%, while many previously used resources (e.g., User_39, User_56, User_84, User_57, User_67, User_96) decreased or disappeared. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007]

statement: The evidence supports a hypothesis that resource allocation changed: activities A01, A03, A11, A13, A14, A17, and A22 became more concentrated on a few resources (notably User_3, User_78, and User_61) instead of being spread across many resources, with A11 becoming exclusively assigned to a single resource. This is directly shown by eight resource-related items (ASSIGN and CONC), far exceeding the 0.006 items expected by chance for that family, and the pattern is consistent across all affected activities. The main limitation is that the control-flow item (DIR001) is a single item against an expected 0.2, so it could be a chance fluctuation and does not by itself support a structural change.
